turns.content: After spatial discretization of a higher-dimensional heat equation, suppose exp(hA) is replaced by a rational approximation R(A)=P(A)/Q(A). What algebraic structure of this evaluation must be exposed before its work can be split across processors?
After factoring Q(z), which algebraic decomposition rewrites R(z) as a sum of simple terms associated with its linear factors?
Translate the resulting terms into shifted linear systems involving A. Why can those systems be solved concurrently?
Distinguish the decomposition step from stability analysis, boundary-condition assumptions, and merely locating the roots of Q.
Describe how a sequential rational-operator evaluation becomes a parallel schedule of independent solves.
If some poles occur as complex-conjugate pairs, does that change the source of parallelism or only the arithmetic used for the independent terms?
State the key algebraic mechanism for the sequential-to-parallel conversion and explain it briefly.
